According to Steam, I've played this for 58 hours - this is how long so far I have waited for this game to download. I'm at 55%. My internet connection is fast and any other game will download rapidly. This game appears to download an installer from steam and then gets the rest of its files form another source. A quick search suggests this is a common complaint and as I've apparently played this for 58 hours there's no chance of a refund. It's just not worth the cost and hassle even with a discount.

10/10 running it on and SSD for very reasonable load times. I have and i7 and GTX1050 TI haven''t had any serious performance drops. For any of my fellow Canadians out their they recently added more detailed scans of a few Canadian cities (check patch notes) and they are shockingly accurate. The only real issue I have is the areas outside of North America, Europe, and australia are not as good. Though because of the current political climate it does make sense. However I would like it if they fleshed out south america and Africa more. But we shall see what they bring in future updates

The graphics are great, its actually a very great sim, but just not my type, i personally prefer DCS. Meandering around in a passenger plane just looking at the ground wasnt for me. If you dont need the excitement of weapons systems this is for you. I will still recommend this game because its gorgeous, just not my style.

Realism and immersion is stunning, can't get enough of that for now.

Overall, I'm very satisfied, and the how to stuff is also on youtube. So the instructor bit is not that important and as what fs is intended for, I'm very impressed.

Leagues ahead of any other competitors in terms of scenery, graphics, and pretty much everything except flight model / plane selection/ cockpit modeling, but that should be fixed with updates and payware planes.

The BIG downside is the constant updates with hundreds of gigs to download, so it makes it a pain for anyone who isn't constantly playing...

Haven't had the time to get everything dialed in graphic wise yet, and I am thoroughly impressed! Don't love the expense on every aircraft out there, understandably labor intensive, but ouch! That would be my only con to it so far! Love the realism! Its everything that everyone says it is!

Yes I would Reccomend MSFS 2020- If you are a flight sim enthusiast on a limited budget & want to fly offline.
I have been using MS FS since the first wire plane which down loaded of stiffy drives.
My first foray into the "real world" of flght simming did not start well.
Bought the full edition on the X box platform. Nothing I did could make it work. got refunded.
Bought the second delux (large price difference between the two platforms) version and had major issues getting it work
Installation said successful but froze everytime on the first screen.
Turns out it was the a game issue but my Laptop issue.
After many hours of search the net and apply changes I eventually ran a command program that repaired broken files within my system that was causing issues. (I am by no means a computer wiz, if fact the opposite)
Patience, much reading and trial and error got me to the point of MSFS 2020 running smoothly.

It was well worth the effort!

I can only comment from the GA side but this game doesn't deserve the word "simulator" in the name. It is better described as Microsoft Flight. The scenery does look great but the aircraft and flight physics are plainly lacking. For the money that this game has generated and the time it has been on the market there is no excuse to not have accurate flight modeling. If you want to just cruise around and look at scenery this game is fine. If you want modeled systems and an actual flight simulator, I'd recommend DCS.

FS2020 offers nothing for Airbus A320 pilots who have invested hardware like the Thrustmaster TCA Officer Airbus series hoping to simulate procedures and routes as the systems are like an idiot port of a Cessna 152 copy-pasted onto an A320neo. While there may be third-party fixes available, the constant need to update the game will eventually lead to even more bugs that require a full re-installation of all 150GB+ and the latest update of the game. While it has amazing graphics for any card that can push 60 fps on high settings at 1080p, it's a really bad flight simulator. The simplicity of X-Plane 11 might be more manageable.

I am going to try to work though; but i already feel buyer remorse and will most likely request a refund and purchase either the STEAM edition , which is cheaper, or GO directly to Xbox/Microsoft to purchase the Full Standard/Deluxe version.

i really love this game, especially saying that from someone who comes from an aviation family. about 2 years ago my uncle bought it for me and i never touched it since about 8-9 months ago and ever since then it has reached my heart. my family too like the fact that im playing this game, since i they want me to become a pilot and continue of my grandpas legacy of aviators. Great game - been spending many hours practising on different planes and the fact that you can fly to literally anywhere in the world makes it so much fun. There are country airports, farm airports and you can also try to find your own house. "Sky" is the limit :p

Runs great on mine Ryzen 5600X + AMD RX6600 XT - get 50-60 frames no issues on 1440p Medium/High settings and the game looks fantastic and butter smooth frames.

Pretty fun.

I don't really consider myself a plane enthusiast, I play with a controller and all assists on, but being able to explore the world is amazing. So many places I definitely would never be able to get to in real life, and I can just explore them here. Pretty amazing what technology can do nowadays.

The fact the world requires internet so heavily, while understandable, is mildly annoying on bad days (Comcast bruh). Also run into some glitchyness with the custom marketplace stuff, but most issues get resolved with a PC restart. Also, near the ground the graphics aren't great (except for at airports) and some stuff is missing entirely (ex Apple Park and the Supreme Court).

Overall I'm having fun, went back and bought the Premium Deluxe upgrade because I wanted the Boeing and SFO enhancement. It's a lot of fun just flying around and exploring.

Maybe wait for a slight price drop or try it out on Xbox Game Pass first though.

Edit: If you have limited internet, make sure you set up the game accordingly, I've apparently used 60gb on Flight Simulator alone in the past 30 days.
Really fun if bored, Realistic, and overall just fun... I do recommend to ask Google or Youtube for help with controls

Flight Heuristics: Remarkable graphics, especially in VR. With 40+ years of flying experience, the flight modeling is somewhat disappointing. Fundamentally the aircraft responds immediately to inputs or turbulence, instead of a quick acceleration to the movement. Metaphorically, it is like at car changing speeds with throttle input immediately instead of accelerating to the throttle position. The air is compressible and therefore there should be a little flow to the movement. Landing is a little unrealistic as there is no response to touchdown (not porpoising which is different). When a prop plane starts, the nose usually dips a little, not just sit there stone still.
These are tiny beefs, and I do enjoy visiting all the places I've flown to using different aircraft. Great fun.

I am really enjoying MSFS and having very few issues with it. However it needs to be noted that there are users who are having difficulties.

Some of this is down to the sim, there are bugs and past releases have re-introduced previously resolved issues. There are bugs that have been there since day and are still to be addressed, however the developers have acknowledged these and they have a published road map detailing this and which they are working towards.

There is a growing community with plenty of free content some of it at payware level, there are also a large number of products in development by 3rd parties. So it looks good for the future of the sim.

Some users are reporting issue with flight models, mainly with commercial jets, as I mainly fly GA I have not experienced this and for me it think they compare favourably with those comparative aircraft in X-plane.

This is now my go to sim. The sim colour, clouds, lighting, scenery and orthos are the next level from the competition and this sim is still in its infancy. To get close to that in X-plane I spend hundreds of pounds on 3rd party scenery, weather upgrades, colour enhances etc. So what you get out of the box, is in my opinion well worth it.

Game itself is good. However the way it is provided is total garbage. Microsoft just being the scummy company they are.
The amount of downsides to having updates be done thrid-party and in-game instead of through steam is higher than the amount of times TX2 was booed at the Download festival, for instance:
- The download takes you 1 hour at the least, and because its ingame, when you can finally play the game you already have "played" half the maximum playtime to refund something, so if you play for a little longer than an hour after you are finally allowed to play and you feel msfs is not really for you, you can't refund it.
- If you want to uninstall msfs through steam, because the main big update files aren't handled by steam, it will only uninstall the initial 2 GB from the launcher. If you want to fully remove the absolute behemoth of gigabytes that is msfs, you'll have to go to a separate folder (%appdata%/Microsoft Flight Simulator/Packages/Official/Steam) and delete the files yourself. Not only is this more tedious, but it makes it harder to uninstall this behemoth to most new players not familiar with this.

Longstory short: Game is good and fun, but it is absolutely weighed down due to the stupid garbage system of not handling updates through steam. If only Microsoft would finally handle updates through steam, this would really become one of the best games in existence, in my opinion (copium).
the game practically requires a flight sim rig and if you dont have that because a good quality cheap one costed 300 $ well then good luck trying to play the game

I don't really understand. When I pre-ordered this game and when it was released, it was simply known as Microsoft Flight Simulator.
The idea was that it would be constantly updated and it would be the ongoing version for the foreseeable future.
In 2022, a "40th Anniversary Update" was added, and the game suddenly changed it's name to "Microsoft Flight Simulator 40th Anniversary Edition"... this wasn't what I originally purchased.

Now, Microsoft have a new version, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

I can't help but feel that I was missold the game. I bought a sim that would be the base game, with DLC, Updates and patches added going forward, but it seems that they have shelved that idea, renamed this version and added a new version of the game that I have to shell out another £70 for...

Don't get me wrong, this version is really good, and I don't have any issues. I just can't help but feel cheated by the game studios when they release a game and concept, rename it 2 years down the line and then replace it for a newer version and charge me for the priveledge. Why isn't it DLC?

the absolute worst launcher experience. to install you have to launch the game and it installs through microsoft (big brain move right?) now you can't get a refund because the in-game install bogs down and adds to your in-game time. now you get no refund after you try it for five minutes once it installs and you decide it's not for you. now you are stuck with it. then you will break out the flight sticks and play it because you bought it at this point no going back, but oh no, you need to update it through the in-game launcher. spoiler alert: it takes forever and you will constantly be stuck on step 1/5: checking for updates. congratulations, you now gave microsoft 60 dollars to own a completely nonexistent gaming experience. game is pretty nifty on the OFF chance you can get the launcher to do it's job and update the game. instead of buying this game: go dig a hole in your yard and burn 60 dollars in that hole to warm your hands for a bit, looking at the flames enveloping your hard earned money in seconds is probably more fun than looking at this awful launcher for several hours.

Badly developed software - generally unreliable - just google to see how often it crashes for everyone.

Regular forced updates completely kill the game for days or weeks until hotfix patches are developed - the most recent being to support XBOX by sacrificing playability for PC Users. Game is not 'complete' and should technically be marked as 'early access' as many features are broken or missing - even a year after initial release.

I've played early access alpha's that were more reliable and more complete, and at least they are a reasonable price.

The main attraction (and the only thing good about it at all) is the scenery is second-to-none, of course that's only when you can actually get the game to work to see it.

Not sure what to say but the fact this game is truly awe inspiring. Honestly I've always been a fan of flight sims but Microsoft flight sim is the best out there. Its got a little of everything for everyone. If you want a more arcade experience you can do that, otherwise if you want more simulation or a challenge you can do that too. Asobo (the devs) are always hard at work and while the game isn't perfect by any means and performance is always a battle, I can say that this game will be updated for a long time. Not only have the devs said they want to update it over the course of 10 years but that along with the community making amazing addons is something that makes me happy to always continue playing and support this giant leap in flight sims.

This game is beyond unstable and every update I find a new reason not to continue playing it. It's been a good while and I think the game is still having glitches and bugs that make it unplayable. Sure, the game is pretty but when it crashes on long haul flights what's the point, not to mention many airports have considerable lag. Go play Xplane

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (78%) on Steam, with players praising the graphics and art.
The most common complaint is bugs and crashes, followed by price and developer updates.

details.text: Recent reviews are more positive than the all-time score, at 83%.
Players with few hours logged are much less positive, at 37%, than long-time players, at 82%.
